comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026-2027 TER defines one 180-EC Liberal Arts and Sciences programme with no formal tracks: a 55-EC Academic Core, a 95-EC Major and a 30-EC Minor. The generic target does not name a Major. The Free Major is the least specialised valid Major because it may combine Humanities, Social Sciences and Sciences, and is therefore selected neutrally before considering UCR fit. The reconstruction preserves all restricted elective and minor space without inventing subjects. A valid 15-EC thesis option is selected in year three.

routeSelection.basis: The TER states that the programme has no tracks and permits Humanities, Social Sciences, Sciences or a Free Major. The Free Major can combine all three disciplines and is therefore the least specialised and most general valid Major; it is selected without reference to UCR fit.

selection.assessment: The closest match owns the defining Liberal Arts and Sciences breadth, individual programme design, interdisciplinary societal challenges, ethical responsibility, sustainability and research core. The health, life-sciences, neuroscience, psychology and AI cluster supports a distinct sciences-oriented curriculum. The politics, philosophy, economics, law and global-business cluster supports a distinct social-sciences curriculum. Arts and Culture remains an evidenced direction but is not attempted after the three-alternative maximum. Curricular-topic rows support these directions; illustrative and outcome rows remain search-only.

alternatives.label: Liberal Arts and Sciences: Society, Culture and Science
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines humanities, social sciences, law, economics, data, psychology and sustainability with quantitative and qualitative research, advanced disciplinary work and independent research.
alternatives.concept: A broad Liberal Arts and Sciences programme that integrates society, culture, politics, law, economics, data, psychology and sustainability around contemporary challenges, supported by quantitative and qualitative research.
progression: Foundational philosophy, history, politics, law, sociology, data and methods precede advanced international relations, ethics, qualitative research, sustainability, media research, governance and a history research seminar. Formal prerequisites occur earlier and all courses are offered in their assigned terms.

alternatives.label: Health, Life Sciences, Neuroscience and Human Behaviour
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is organised around human biology, health, disease, brain, cognition and behaviour, with statistics, philosophy of mind and advanced empirical research.
alternatives.distinctness: Twenty-one courses differ from the broad Liberal Arts and Sciences curriculum. This route replaces most of its politics, law, history, culture and sustainability content with a sustained biomedical, neuroscience, psychology and health sequence.
alternatives.concept: A sciences-oriented Liberal Arts and Sciences programme combining molecular and biomedical science with neuroscience, psychology, cognition, health and empirical research.
progression: The life-and-health and brain-and-behaviour gateways precede molecular biology, physiology, biochemistry, psychology and cognition, followed by advanced pharmacology, pathology, neuroscience, disease, research and psychodiagnostics. Formal prerequisites occur earlier and all courses are offered in their assigned terms.
traceOverrides: examines philosophical problems of mind, cognition and consciousness as a direct complement to the neuroscience and human-behaviour curriculum

alternatives.label: Politics, Philosophy, Economics, Law and Global Business
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines political philosophy, comparative and international politics, law, economics, history, sociology and communication, with quantitative and qualitative research.
alternatives.distinctness: Sixteen courses differ from the broad curriculum and twenty-three differ from the health-sciences route. The curriculum concentrates on politics, philosophy, economics, law and global business rather than broad cross-domain exploration or biomedical science.
alternatives.concept: A social-sciences Liberal Arts and Sciences programme organised around political institutions, law, markets, global business, justice and international order.
progression: Introductory political philosophy, comparative politics, law, economics, history and methods precede international relations, public and international law, behavioural economics, public economics, econometrics, EU politics and advanced research. Formal prerequisites occur earlier and all courses are offered in their assigned terms.

examines persuasion, framing and ethics in public and institutional decision-making

notes.text: Both institutions offer Liberal Arts and Sciences, but their formal structures differ. Groningen combines a 55-EC Academic Core, a 95-EC Major and a 30-EC Minor with three annual projects and a 15-EC thesis option. UCR organises 24 courses through an open curriculum with Personal & Professional Development and optional independent research rather than a fixed major/core/minor template.
